A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. It results from an extra factor of $10^{-3}$ error when converting $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.

B.explanation: Correct. $W = p\Delta V$ with $p = 101000\text{ Pa}$ and $\Delta V = 4.00 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$ gives $0.404\text{ J} = 404\text{ mJ}$.

C.explanation: Numerically $101 \times 4 = 404$ but units are wrong. It multiplies $101$ by $4$ without converting $\text{kPa}$ to $\text{Pa}$ and $\text{cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$.

D.explanation: Far too large. It treats the $4.00\text{ cm}^3$ volume change as if it were much larger in $\text{m}^3$, ignoring the $10^{-6}$ conversion.

hints: Notice the gas pushes the syringe plunger out against atmospheric pressure, so use $p = 101\text{ kPa}$ and volume change $\Delta V = 6.00 - 2.00 = 4.00\text{ cm}^3$.
Connect this to work done at constant pressure: $W = p\Delta V$, which needs $p$ in $\text{Pa}$ and $\Delta V$ in $\text{m}^3$ to give $W$ in $\text{J}$.
Convert $4.00\text{ cm}^3$ to $\text{m}^3$ using $1\text{ cm}^3 = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$, then multiply by $101000\text{ Pa}$ and check whether the result is closest to micro-, milli- or whole joules.
walkthrough: Identify the process: the heated gas expands and does work pushing back the atmosphere at constant atmospheric pressure $p = 101\text{ kPa} = 101000\text{ Pa}$.
Find the volume change from the syringe volumes: $\Delta V = 6.00 - 2.00 = 4.00\text{ cm}^3$.
State the rule for constant-pressure expansion: $W = p\Delta V$.
Convert the volume change to SI units: $\Delta V = 4.00\text{ cm}^3 = 4.00 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3$ because $1\text{ m}^3 = 10^6\text{ cm}^3$.
Substitute with units: $W = (1.01 \times 10^5\text{ Pa})(4.00 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3) = 0.404\text{ J}$.
Check units and size: $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^3 = \text{J}$, and $0.404\text{ J} = 404 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 404\text{ mJ}$. This is option B.
